newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto agrees on state banks merger.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto agrees on state banks merger.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto had principally agreed on moves to merge the country's state banks to improve their competitiveness, Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Friday.
"Suharto has been fully informed and principally he agrees on such a move (to merge state banks)," Mar'ie told reporters after meeting Suharto.
"What is left now is the technical details on which banks will be merged. There is a possibility affiliated banks could emerge. That's also possible. We are preparing it (the policy)," Mar'ie said.
The minister however added that would take some time to finalise details but gave no time-frame.
The World Bank said in a recent report that Indonesia needed to improve its financial institutions to meet possible macroeconomic shocks.

The bank suggested interim measures were likely to be necessary to improve state banks' corporate governance and performance such as closures, mergers and downsizing, perhaps in conjunction with unbundling and sale of some activities.
Bisnis Indonesia daily reported earlier the government planned to merge its seven state banks into four entities.
It said PT Bank Negara Indonesia, PT Bank Expor Impor Indonesia, PT Bank Dagang Negara and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia would emerge from the consolidation.
The daily did not say which banks the other three state banks -- PT Bank Tabungan Negara, PT Bank Pembangunan Indonesia and PT Bank Bumi Daya -- would merge with.

Financial markets have long anticipated the move. Brokers and dealers have said the government was planning to merge its state banks to make them more effective to face free trade agreements which will be implemented by 2003 under a plan prepared by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam are the current members of ASEAN. Burma, Laos and Cambodia are scheduled to join this year.
